input: capacity is a nonnegative safe integer. Each trip is [passengers,start,end], with nonnegative integer passengers and 0 <= start < end <= 1000000000. The sum P of all passenger counts is at most 9007199254740991. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt; separately declared probabilities are finite primitive Number.
return: Boolean indicating whether all trips can be served without exceeding capacity, interpreting each trip as active on half-open [start,end), so drop-offs free capacity before pickups at the same position.
mutation_aliasing: All input arrays and trip rows remain unchanged; local signed endpoint deltas and sorted coordinates are private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Every per-position partial delta is within [-P,P] and onboard count within [0,P], so all arithmetic is exact. Comparator differences are bounded by 1000000000. Aggregating simultaneous events implements half-open semantics without an ordering ambiguity. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n log(n + 1) + 1) time and O(n + 1) auxiliary space for n trips, counting endpoint map, copied key array and sort workspace. Hash-table and comparison-sort assumptions are explicit. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.
